title: Moneyflow repaired absorption and first-passage feature candidates
summary: Moneyflow V15/V18/V19 did not produce a standalone official alpha, but preserved reusable feature candidates around profit-payer supply, repaired absorption, and first-passage payoff geometry.

mechanism.payer: profit payers, forced sellers, uninformed liquidity demand, or pressure-driven institutions
mechanism.receiver: latent informed absorption or patient capital
mechanism.random_object: hidden-state price process and first-passage payoff
mechanism.math_forced_insight: The first-passage payoff forced the research away from additive net-inflow scoring: a long signal must separate repaired absorption from crowded chase by comparing upside hit probability and distance against downside barrier risk and turnover cost.

evidence.falsification: V21 full IS showed positive gross excess but turnover costs exceeded gross edge; do not promote as standalone.

relations.note: Moneyflow long edge is defined as upside repair hitting probability times distance minus downside break probability times distance and cost.
The desired long side buys supply from profit payers or forced sellers after absorption confirmation.
V19/V21 preserved gross information but standalone after-cost long NAV failed.
Net inflow or main-buy strength alone cannot distinguish smart absorption from crowded chase.
Use V18b/V19d as model-combination features or inspiration, not as official standalone alphas.

reuse_guidance: When a new factor has profit-payer supply or repaired reversal logic, retrieve this node first.
Do not compress a hitting/path-repair problem into only mean, sigma, or z-score.
Do not promote positive Rank IC unless long-side after-cost evidence clears turnover cost.
Use V18b as the preferred first-passage mathematical template.
